The '''55th [[Golden Globe Award]]s''', honoring the best in [[film]] and television for 1997, were held on January 18, 1998.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sterngold|first1=David|title='Titanic' Wins Top Golden Globe Award|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/01/19/movies/titanic-wins-top-golden-globe-award.html|access-date=11 January 2018|work=The New York Times|date=19 January 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Lowry|first1=Brian|title=Their Ship Sails In|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-jan-19-ca-9758-story.html|access-date=11 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 January 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Golden Globe Winners|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-jan-19-ca-10004-story.html|access-date=11 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 January 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Titanic sweeps Golden Globes|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/48591.stm|access-date=11 January 2018|work=BBC News|date=19 January 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title='Titanic' cruises Golden Globes|url=http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9801/19/golden.globes.final/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010721153659/http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9801/19/golden.globes.final/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 21, 2001|access-date=11 January 2018|work=CNN|date=19 January 1998}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title='Titanic' grabs top Golden Globe honors|url=http://chronicle.augusta.com/stories/1998/01/19/ent_220845.shtml|access-date=11 January 2018|work=The Augusta Chronicle|date=19 January 1998}}</ref> The nominations were announced on December 18, 1997.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wallace|first1=Amy|last2=Welkos|first2=Robert|title=Studio Films Resurface With 'Titanic' Surge|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-dec-19-ca-54-story.html|access-date=11 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 December 1997}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Complete List of Golden Globe Nominees|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-dec-19-ca-57-story.html|access-date=11 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 December 1997}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Nominees for Golden Globe Awards|url=http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9712/18/golden.globes.list/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030325221501/http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/9712/18/golden.globes.list/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 25, 2003|access-date=11 January 2018|work=CNN|date=18 December 1997}}</ref> The ceremony was watched by 24.3 million viewers, a record at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jamshowbiz.com/TelevisionRatings/us.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040203065228/http://www.jamshowbiz.com/TelevisionRatings/us.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2004-02-03|title=Golden Globes set NBC ratings record|date=January 28, 2004|publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

== Memorable ceremony moments ==
The ceremony at the [[The Beverly Hilton|Beverly Hilton]] was notable for two memorable moments. First, when Christine Lahti was announced as the winner of Best Actress in a Television Drama, she was in the restroom and came out a few minutes later to accept. Also, after winning Best Actor in a Movie or Miniseries, Ving Rhames brought fellow nominee Jack Lemmon on stage to give his award to the elder actor.
